description: All 24 nbrm.mk candidates are recorded from search-engine evidence only; none could be opened directly because of the domain-wide 403.
I identified landing pages but not the underlying PDF/XLS document URLs (one exception observed: /content/Annual_Report_2020.pdf, implying a /content/ document root).

This cell is a POINTER cell but its registers were not opened, so the actual named entities (payment institutions, e-money institutions, payment system operators, savings houses, exchange offices) were not enumerated. Only the bank list was recoverable indirectly via secondary sources.

Bank disclosure in MK is also driven by the Official Gazette (Службен весник) and by the Securities and Exchange Commission / Macedonian Stock Exchange for listed banks — outside this cell's boundary but load-bearing for 'disclosures / investor relations / earnings' topics.
The payment-institutions register page slug remains unfound (see negative finding).

MSE issuer-page slugs confirmed for only 3 of the listed banks (Komercijalna, NLB, UNI Banka). Stopanska (STB), Halkbank, Sparkasse, TTK, Centralna kooperativna and Razvojna banka slugs remain unresolved.
No confirmed structured API for SEI-Net; RSS gives headlines and links but the document bodies require rendering.
KHV monthly-report ID pattern is only anchored on one confirmed point (izvestaj67 = May 2012). The current ID range and whether older/newer reports use the same scheme is unknown.

The National Bank of RNM (НБРСМ / nbrm.mk) was touched only incidentally via a CDHV reference; it is the prudential supervisor and publishes bank-level supervisory and financial data that complements exchange disclosures.
No Albanian-language search performed (out of declared run scope mk/en).
Albanian-language (sq) association and chamber sources were not systematically searched.

Payment-specific industry bodies (card scheme national forums, an ATM/POS operators grouping, or a payment institutions association under the Law on Payment Services and Payment Systems) were not identified. Only KIBS (as an MBA member institution) surfaced as a payments-infrastructure actor.

For most association sources the existence of publications is established but the concrete artefact URLs (White Book editions, MiCreS newsletter PDFs, chamber annual reports after 2010, DMWV member directories for other years) were not enumerated.

MASIT's full current membership (13+ pages of paginated profiles) and AmCham's and FIC's member lists were sampled, not enumerated. The bank-technology supplier layer is therefore only partially mapped.

Association event materials (conference agendas, sponsor lists, presentation decks) — historically the richest indirect reveal of vendor-bank relationships — were identified as a category but no concrete deck or agenda repository was located.

Business Confederation of Macedonia and the European Business Association (both named in a US government listing of principal MK business associations) were surfaced but not investigated; the Сојуз на стопански комори website could not be confirmed live.

For UJP, the exact stable index page listing all e-Faktura technical specifications and API documentation was not pinned down; only one deep PDF path and the general announcements area were confirmed via search.

Other state/quasi-state financial bodies in the same actor family were not covered in this slice: Customs Administration (Царинска управа), Central Registry (Централен регистар), State Foreign Exchange Inspectorate / Financial Police (Финансиска полиција), Public Procurement Bureau (e-nabavki) and the Securities & Exchange / MAPAS supervisors.
English-language mirrors of the MK state sources were only spot-checked (finance.gov.mk en-GB, dzr.mk English branding); it is unknown how complete or how delayed the English versions are.
APIs were identified in principle (MakStat PX-Web JSON-stat, data.gov.mk catalogue, UJP e-Invoice integration API) but none were exercised.
Historical depth of each publication series (how far back annual reports, audit reports and FIU reports go online) was not established.
Broadcast media (Telma, Sitel, Kanal 5, Alsat, MRT) economy segments were not directly enumerated; only glimpsed indirectly via the GRID.mk aggregator.
Consumer-complaint channels beyond journalism (bank ombudsman-style reporting, consumer-organisation statements, Facebook consumer groups) are unmapped in this cell.
Archive depth per outlet is unknown; only emagazin.mk was observed to keep a separate historic archive.
English-language MK-domestic reporting is thin in this cell; only regional wires (SeeNews, Bloomberg Adria) and a claimed bilingual daily were identified.
The cell is almost entirely indirect/pointer by design; the one direct source found (Provizii.mk fee database) suggests other structured MK-language data products may exist unmapped.

Parent-group IR channels beyond NLB and ProCredit were not covered: Steiermärkische Sparkasse (Sparkasse Bank Skopje), Halkbank T.A.O. (Halkbank AD Skopje), OTP/Alpha-related entities, and Stopanska Banka's owner NBG legacy structures.
Payments-side international trackers are thin: card schemes (Visa/Mastercard CEE press), acquirers/PSPs, and fintech-market trackers covering MK were only lightly sampled.
Structured statistical aggregators (World Bank Global Findex, IMF Financial Access Survey, ECB/BIS payments statistics) were not enumerated as machine-readable series for MK.
No archival strategy identified for paywalled wires (SeeNews, bne IntelliNews) whose historical items are the main English record of MK bank earnings before ~2015.
No local-language (mk) source belongs in this cell by construction, so the cell contributes nothing to MK-language coverage.

Careers pages were confirmed only for Stopanska Banka; the remaining MK banks (Komercijalna, NLB, Sparkasse, Halkbank, ProCredit, Silk Road, UNIBanka, Centralna kooperativna, ALTA, TTK, Kapital, Development Bank) and PSPs need their own careers-URL discovery.
Albanian-language (sq) hiring, complaint and event channels were not searched, although a large share of MK banking customers and some bank communications are in Albanian (CaSys itself supports sq).
Public procurement / tender notices (e-nabavki) were not covered in this cell but are a strong indirect signal for system purchases by state-owned or public-sector-adjacent financial institutions.
Job ads and event pages expire quickly and are frequently deleted; without archiving, the historical hiring signal is unrecoverable.
LinkedIn holds the densest platform-naming hiring signal but is ToS-restricted and auth-walled, so it cannot enter the automated pipeline.

Per-issuer archival file stores were mapped only for Stopanska banka Skopje, NLB and Alta; the remaining MK banks (Komercijalna banka, Sparkasse, ProCredit, Halkbank, TTK, Uni banka, Silk Road, Centralna kooperativna, Development Bank of North Macedonia/МБПР) and savings houses have not had their PDF paths enumerated.

No archival layer was mapped for the Комисија за хартии од вредност (Securities and Exchange Commission) or the Фонд за осигурување на депозити (Deposit Insurance Fund), both of which publish historical annual reports and decisions relevant to bank disclosure.
No archival source was mapped for MK payments infrastructure operators (KIBS, CaSys, MIPS/MIPS-participant reporting), whose historical volume reporting is the backbone of any payments time series.

Albanian-language (sq) sources were out of the declared run languages (mk, en) and were not searched, although a substantial share of MK banking communication and academic work is published in Albanian.
No proactive archiving of currently-live MK IR pages has been established, so pages pruned between runs will be lost if Internet Archive has not independently captured them.
Not every NBRSM-licensed bank was reached in this pass. Silk Road Banka's own site, and any remaining smaller/savings institutions (штедилници), were not opened.
Document examples collected span scattered years (2012, 2016-2018, 2021-2025) rather than a verified continuous series per bank; no per-bank inventory of which years are actually posted.
No measurement of English-version availability or publication lag on any MK bank IR page.
None of these bank IR sections was observed to offer RSS, an API, or a dated index; discovery of new filings depends on polling.

Capital notices (докапитализација, издавање акции, subordinated debt) and takeover/public-offer documents were only glimpsed indirectly (MSE 'Јавни понуди за преземање' repository paths, e.g. Sparkasse and TTK takeover folders); no bank-site capital-notice page was mapped.
Robots.txt, terms of use and rate-limit posture were not checked for any of these bank domains.
No confirmed URL for the Steiermärkische Sparkasse annual report (Geschäftsbericht) or for any Sparkasse-group segment disclosure covering North Macedonia.
NBG (parent of Stopanska Banka) IR entry point not confirmed; no quarterly results-presentation URL captured.

Local-language (mk) discovery was performed but produced results concentrated on one issuer (Stopanska banka). MK-language IR/шеаreholder-assembly material for NLB Banka Skopje, Sparkasse Bank AD Skopje, Halkbank AD Skopje and CCB Skopje was not systematically enumerated.

Exchange-level disclosure platforms for three parents were identified only by inference and not exercised: LJSE SEOnet (NLB), KAP (Halkbank), Bulgarian Stock Exchange / x3news (CCB Sofia, Chimimport).

Rating-agency and IFI channels were not covered: Fitch/Moody's/S&P rating actions on MK subsidiaries usually rest on parent-support assessments and contain MK-specific analysis, and EBRD/IFC are minority shareholders in Stopanska Banka with their own project disclosure.
Smaller foreign-linked MK banks (e.g. UNIBanka/Universal Investment Bank, TTK Banka, Development Bank of North Macedonia) were not traced to any foreign parent group in this run.
The commercial terms, data catalogue and technical interface (API vs. web ordering) of the ЦРРСМ Дистрибутивен систем are not documented in anything retrievable without a session or a contract.

This pass did not enumerate the actual MK banking and payments legal entities (banks, савings houses, payment institutions, e-money institutions, processors, POS/ATM vendors) with their ЕМБС numbers, so the statutory-filing channels have no target list yet.
Albanian-language coverage was not attempted, although crm.com.mk serves an /sq/ locale and a material share of MK financial-sector actors and their communications are Albanian-language.
How far back the Register of Annual Accounts and the publications feed are retrievable (earliest available filing year, whether pre-digital filings are scanned) was not established.

The Law on the Central Registry restricts use of published register data to personal, non-commercial purposes. Whether internal market-intelligence use by a commercial firm falls inside or outside that restriction is unresolved.

Other statutory archive channels adjacent to the registrar were only touched (Official Gazette free-issue archive structure, the Public Revenue Office's published lists, the Securities and Exchange Commission's filings for AD banks).
Payment institutions and e-money institutions licensed in MK were not individually enumerated because the NBRM register page was 403-blocked in this pass.
No tender/procurement channel was scouted for payments-infrastructure contracts (e.g. e-nabavki public procurement portal for NBRM, KIBS or state-bank switch/ATM/POS tenders).

Supranational/aggregator views of MK payments infrastructure (ECB/IMF/World Bank Global Payment Systems Survey, EBRD, CPMI Red Book-style country notes, Western Balkans payments-integration reports) were not scouted in this pass.
No archival strategy identified for operator pages whose news listings are JS-rendered and not paginated (kibs.mk, casys.com.mk).
The Macedonian Banking Association (Здружение на банкарството) was referenced only second-hand as a CaSys partner; its own site and publications were not opened.

Bank-owned wallets and acquirers (HalkPay, NLB Pay, Komercijalna, Stopanska, Uni Banka acquiring) were identified as actors but their individual newsroom URLs were not enumerated one by one in this pass.
LinkedIn company pages — in practice the primary launch/partnership channel for small MK payment firms — were not scouted, and are ToS-restricted for automated collection.
Crypto/VASP-adjacent payment actors and BNPL providers in MK were not covered; the SEPA accession angle (MK joining SEPA) was seen only in passing via a World Bank item.
Albanian-language (sq) payment/fintech PR aimed at MK's Albanian-speaking market was not searched at all; the run scope specified only mk and en.

Only a handful of the ~13 MK banks appear anywhere in vendor material: NLB Banka Skopje, Komercijalna Banka, Stopanska Banka, Halkbank. Sparkasse Bank, ProCredit, TTK, Centralna kooperativna, Silk Road, Development Bank and others have no vendor-side trace found.
ATM/self-service hardware vendors (NCR Atleos, Diebold Nixdorf, GRG, Hyosung) and their MK distributors are essentially unmapped beyond Printec.
Confirmed MK scheme/vendor items cluster in 2020-2021 (Mastercard digital ID, Halkbank wallet) with only a few recent MK-media items. 2023-2026 vendor activity is under-covered.

Vendor and scheme LinkedIn/Facebook pages (Nextsense, ASEE Macedonia, CaSys, Printec MK) were seen in results but not assessed as sources; in MK these carry deployment announcements that never reach the corporate site.

No vendor-side route was found into private-bank procurement decisions beyond voluntary marketing; state-owned or state-adjacent institutions (Development Bank of North Macedonia) may publish tenders that name banking-technology vendors.

State-owned enterprises and public funds that are large payment buyers — ЕСМ (power utility), Македонски железници, Фонд за здравствено осигурување (ФЗОМ), Фонд за ПИОМ, Управа за јавни приходи (UJP), Царинска управа, Македонска пошта, водоводни ЈП and public transport (ЈСП Скопје) — were not individually researched in this pass.

No CPV-code-driven search was executed (66100000 банкарски и инвестициски услуги, 66110000, 66172000 обработка на трансакции, 66600000 трезорски услуги, 30162000/POS equipment, 48440000 финансиски софтвер).

The ESJN is an ASP.NET WebForms application whose notice search relies on postbacks; no attempt was made to establish whether an API, RSS feed or bulk export exists, and no robots.txt or terms-of-use review was done.

Albanian-language procurement publications (Agjencia/Byroja e prokurimeve publike, njoftim për prokurim publik, shërbime bankare) were not searched, although Albanian is an official language and many municipalities publish bilingually.

Other IFI/donor channels touching MK financial infrastructure were not covered: IFC, KfW/GIZ (only referenced indirectly), UNDP MK procurement, EU IPA/EU Delegation to North Macedonia calls, and the Council of Europe Development Bank.
No assessment was made of how far back the ESJN public archive, the executed-contracts register or the Appeals Commission decisions go, nor of retention/purge behaviour.

Bank supplier-onboarding routes (vendor registration forms, e-sourcing tools such as SAP Ariba/Coupa instances used by parent groups OTP, NLB, Steiermärkische, Halkbank Türkiye, ProCredit Holding) were not located for the MK subsidiaries.
Whether any aggregator genuinely indexes private-buyer RFPs in MK remains untested behind paywalls.

Non-web private notice channels — print/online newspaper classifieds (Нова Македонија, Слободен печат), LinkedIn posts by bank procurement staff, and bank ESG/annual-report supplier sections — were not covered in this pass.
Local terminology for private-sector solicitation is unsettled: 'јавен повик' and 'оглас' are dominated by state and employment usage, making them very noisy for private procurement retrieval.
